title: the-web-server-graduates-to-starlette
intention: Replace the stdlib http.server web_server with Starlette + uvicorn. The graft source is TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py — already built, already proven. The graduation brings async, WebSocket fan-out, and static file serving.
why: The trouble panel (and every future dynamic pane) needs client-side interaction and server push. The stdlib web_server is synchronous and cannot do either. This is not a new dependency decision — the framework was chosen in February and built in TheIgors.
traces_to: Law 8 — nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass. The graft from TheIgors is bytes crossing from a sibling project; the graft ticket and proof are owed.
Law 4 — the framework was CHOSEN in February and confirmed by Akien; this is enforcement of that ruling, not a new decision.
one-web-server-surfaces-in-the-shim — ONE web server; a device gets a declared PANE, never its own route/port/server. This replaces, it does not add.

falsifier.proves_green: The stdlib http.server is replaced by Starlette + uvicorn. THREE things must hold: (1) existing pane URLs render identically — no regression on current surfaces; (2) WebSocket connection establishes and can receive a server push — the capability the current server lacks; (3) the listener is Starlette's ASGI app run by uvicorn, not custom socket code — the device logic (routing in server.py, rendering in render.py) stays where it is and does not leak into the transport.
falsifier.proves_red: RED if: (1) a second web server appears — the one-web-server rule is the standing constraint; (2) device logic (routing, rendering) leaks into the transport layer — server.py and render.py are the logic, Starlette is the transport; (3) existing pane URLs break — a regression is a red, not a tolerable transition cost; (4) the graft introduces dependencies not already in TheIgors' utility_closet_server.py without justification; (5) the graft enters without a graft ticket and proof (Law 8 — bytes are a graft with a ticket and proof, ideas are free and cited in the charter's entry).
falsifier.horizon: Before the-cairn-device-owns-the-trouble-panel — that ticket depends on this one for WebSocket capability. No blockers for this build; the graft source exists on disk and the framework is confirmed.

linked_ideas: Akien 2026-08-19: framework question on the trouble panel; Starlette confirmed as the ruled framework (CC's recommendation Feb 2026, Akien confirmed same session)

questions.a: This is a GRAFT from a sibling project, not a greenfield framework selection. The graft ticket and proof are owed (Law 8).
The shape (route -> fetch device DATA -> render) is already proven in the current web_server. What changes is the transport and the ability to push updates.
ONE web server — the rule holds. This replaces the current one, it does not add a second.
The listener (the socket binding) stays thin — Starlette's ASGI is the new listener, uvicorn is the runner. The device logic (routing, rendering) stays in server.py and render.py.

how: Replace stdlib http.server with Starlette + uvicorn. Graft source: TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py (already built + tested). One graft, one proof, one VALIDATION.

chart_notes.orient: The graft source is TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py. The current web_server is at cairn/cairn/devices/web_server/ — server.py has routing, render.py has rendering, __init__.py has the listener. chart_notes.constrain: OUT: new routes or endpoints (this replaces the transport, not the routing); new dependencies beyond starlette/uvicorn; touching device logic in server.py or render.py beyond the interface change. IN: the ASGI app, uvicorn as runner, WebSocket hub from the graft, static file serving.
chart_notes.validate: Every existing pane URL renders identically before and after (screenshot comparison or content hash). A WebSocket connection to the server establishes and receives at least one push. uvicorn serves the ASGI app and the process is the same single web server process.

decisions.text: starlette 1.6.0 and uvicorn 0.52.4 are ALREADY installed in the venv every cairn command runs under, $HOME/.cairn/venv (interpreter $HOME/.cairn/venv/bin/python3; measured 2026-09-17 by $HOME/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 -c 'import starlette,uvicorn;print(starlette.__version__,uvicorn.__version__)'). Nothing is installed by this build. If a fresh box lacks them the one command is $HOME/.cairn/venv/bin/pip install starlette uvicorn — no activation step. httpx is NOT installed and not needed: the proof drives the ASGI app in-process over raw scopes. No other package enters.
decisions.step: unlisted: Install starlette and uvicorn packages

decisions.text: NOTHING IS WRITTEN OR TRANSLATED IN THIS STEP: the listener is ALREADY BUILT and committed — cairn/devices/web_server/listener.py at commit bc8eb273, unchanged at HEAD 7cf3e513 — and that file IS the deliverable; the builder reads it and changes nothing. What it holds, as built: module docstring (lines 1-5) naming '72e8e3509287' and 'utility_closet_server.py'; imports Request from starlette.requests, Response from starlette.responses, Starlette from starlette.applications, Route and WebSocketRoute from starlette.routing, WebSocket from starlette.websockets, and (line 44) connect_system, harbor_source from cairn.tools.bus_client; module globals _device (a WebServerDevice) and _bus, both set in main(); _ws_clients (a list of accepted websockets); async def _handle_get(request): status, content_type, body = _device.serve(request.url.path); return Response(body, status_code=status, media_type=content_type); async def _handle_post(request): raw = (await request.body()).decode('utf-8', errors='replace'); status, content_type, body = _device.serve(request.url.path, method='POST', body=raw); return Response(body, status_code=status, media_type=content_type); async def _handle_ws_troubles(websocket): await websocket.accept(); append it to _ws_clients; send the JSON list the bus returns for to='trouble' verb='live' (the live trouble list) as one text frame; on disconnect remove it from _ws_clients. The path handed to serve() is request.url.path — the catch-all parameter is never read. _make_app() returns Starlette(routes=[WebSocketRoute('/ws/troubles', _handle_ws_troubles), Route('/{path:path}', _handle_get, methods=['GET']), Route('/{path:path}', _handle_post, methods=['POST'])]). main(argv): argparse with --port (default 80) and --bind (default 0.0.0.0); _bus, heartbeat = connect_system(devices=['ground_loop', 'librarian', 'trouble']) (cairn/tools/bus_client/bus_client.py line 132 — returns (bus, loop), the loop is the heartbeat; no GroundLoop is instantiated, nothing is imported from ground_loop); _device = WebServerDevice(heartbeat, harbor_source=harbor_source(), port=args.port) (harbor_source at bus_client.py line 142); print one '[web_server] serving on http://<bind>:<port>' line; then asyncio.run(server.serve()) where server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(app, host=args.bind, port=args.port, log_level='warning')) — .run() is NOT used. This _bus/_device wiring is what the pre-graft listener already did and it does not change. No rendering, no markup, no device logic in the transport. From /home/akien/dev/src/TheIgors/lab/claudecode/utility_closet_server.py (exists on disk, measured 2026-09-17) only the wiring pattern was taken — Starlette app + Route/WebSocketRoute binding + uvicorn.Config/Server — never its handlers, models or state; TheIgors is not consulted again.
decisions.step: unlisted: Replace listener.py with Starlette/uvicorn ASGI pattern from TheIgors

decisions.text: NOTHING TO IMPLEMENT: the proofs are already built. The standing proofs (test_web_server.py, test_web_server_chat.py, test_web_server_views.py, test_voyage_pane.py under cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/) exercise WebServerDevice.serve() without a socket and pass unchanged, because serve()'s contract is untouched. test_web_server.py additionally carries, since commit 6c233e3c, five teeth declared in its module-level PROVES = {'72e8e3509287': {'1': 'test_there_is_one_web_server', '2': 'test_device_logic_stays_out_of_the_transport', '3': 'test_existing_pane_urls_render_identically_through_the_asgi_app', '4': 'test_the_graft_brings_no_dependency_beyond_its_source', '5': 'test_the_graft_carries_its_ticket_and_proof'}} — one per falsifier clause; each is a function in that file and _main runs every tooth printing PASS/FAIL per name. The builder's whole act here is to run it twice: PYTHONPATH=. $HOME/.cairn/venv/bin/python3 cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py (exit 0 = green). Green twice at HEAD; 4 of 5 red against the pre-graft listener (bc8eb273^).

decisions.text: NO NEW VALIDATION FILE: the validation is the existing cairn/devices/web_server/validations/test_web_server.json, which the tester overwrites in place beside the proof. Sequence, in this order, all from the repo root with PYTHONPATH=. under $HOME/.cairn/venv/bin/python3: (i) the BUILDME crossing is emitted by CC through cairn.tools.base.transitions.emit(..., ticket='72e8e3509287', proven_by='cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py') — proven_by is a keyword argument CC passes on the crossing; nothing sets it automatically; (ii) python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --seal --timeout 600 cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py runs the proof under the tester and writes the seal (verdict 'green'|'red', source_fingerprint, fingerprint_closure, isolation); (iii) python3 -m cairn.devices.tester.cli --hollow 72e8e3509287 --seal cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py reverts the ticket's build to the commit standing at its BUILDME crossing, reruns the proof, and lands ONLY evidence.hollow['72e8e3509287'] (the per-file red reading) onto the standing seal — it does not re-run the proof green, which is why (ii) precedes it. The tester CLI is cairn/devices/tester/cli.py (main at line 325); its flags are --seal (persist the validation), --hollow <ticket> (take the hollow reading), --timeout <seconds>, -q; the validation's location is fixed by the tester — validations/<proof stem>.json beside the proof's proofs/ directory — and no flag moves it. Schema is the tester's standard seal, the same every validations/*.json in the repo carries.

decisions.text: SETTLES D6's crossing (MEASURED 2026-09-24 on c62df2454322, which crossed BUILDME and PROVEME with exactly this shape): CC emits every crossing, never the builder, and the builder never waits on one mid-build. The call is transitions.emit(workflow_str, target, *, history_path, state_path, node_class_root=<default>, **journal_extra) — workflow_str is the ticket's live workflow_and_state; target is 'BUILDME' or 'PROVEME'; history_path='cairn/devices/web_server/history.json'; state_path='cairn/devices/web_server/state.json'; actor='CC', ticket='72e8e3509287', note=<one sentence> and proven_by ride in **journal_extra. emit RETURNS the new cursor string and writes nothing to the ticket: CC writes it back with cairn.tools.artifact.artifact.write(<ticket path>, <json with workflow_and_state replaced>, verb='cast', why=<sentence>). Order: (1) CC rehearses clean at TICKETME:waiting and crosses BUILDME; (2) the builder runs D6(ii) onward — the tester commands; (3) CC rehearses again at BUILDME:waiting (the BUILDME write changed the bytes); (4) CC crosses PROVEME with proven_by='cairn/devices/web_server/proofs/test_web_server.py' — the measured c62 crossing passed proven_by on PROVEME, and that is the form this ticket uses; D6(i)'s wording of proven_by on the BUILDME call is superseded by this line.
